newsitem.title: USA: IMF board approves new emergency fund.
newsitem.headline: IMF board approves new emergency fund.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said Monday its executive board approved a $48 billion line of credit to be used in situations that could threaten the stability of the world monetary system.

The decision to approve the New Arrangements to Borrow follows agreement by 25 potential participants on the terms and conditions in which they will be prepared to make loans to the IMF when emergency resources are needed, the Fund said.

The decision will enter into force when it has been adhered to by participants with credit arrangements amounting to no less than $41 billion, including five members or institutions with the largest credit arrangements.
The decision will remain in effect for five years and may be renewed.

The participants are Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, the Bundesbank, Finland, France, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Kuwait, Luxembourg, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Norway, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Spain, Sveriges Riksbank, the Swiss National Bank, Thailand, Britain and the United States.

The NAB will not replace the General Arrangments to Borrow, a pool of funds that remains in force, but the IMF said the New Arrangments will be the facility to be used first and the principal resource in the event the funds are needed.
The decision was hailed by IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus, but he made clear that the new pool of funds cannot be used as a substitute for the strengthening of quotas.
